summary.headline: Diamond Power Q2 FY27 revenue crossed INR1,000 crore at INR1,032 crore (up 135% YoY), with PAT of INR108 crore and net worth turned positive.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR1,032 crore, up 135% YoY and 50% QoQ, with EBITDA (incl. other income) of INR133 crore at a 12.9% margin and PAT of INR108 crore versus INR28 crore a year ago. Management attributed part of the growth to aluminium and copper price pass-through, estimating about one-third of revenue growth is metal and price variation, and pointed to a new data centre copper cable line contributing INR242 crore (23% of revenue). The balance sheet swung to positive net worth of INR764 crore and net cash of INR572 crore after the INR1,614 crore QIP and full repayment of promoter loans. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR4,300-4,500 crore, implying INR2,580 crore in H2.

segments.name: Medium voltage (MV) and EHV cables
segments.commentary: Cables were 40% of Q2 revenue; 11 kV and 33 kV cables made up 79% of cable revenue outside data centre, with 33 kV the largest product line. MV cables are INR1,328 crore (36%) of order book.

segments.name: Conductors (AL59, ECO, HTLS)
segments.commentary: Conductors were 31% of Q2 revenue; 46% of order book (about INR1,718 crore), including a INR974 crore AL59 order for an 800 kV HVDC line. Dispatches were 6,850 km in the quarter.

segments.name: Data centre cables
segments.commentary: New copper cable line contributed INR242 crore (23% of Q2 revenue), up from zero three months earlier; INR240 crore delivered in September alone. Management expects about INR750 crore from data centre customers in FY27.

segments.name: Solar cables (3.3 kV)
segments.commentary: Solar cables were INR39 crore in Q2 and INR221 crore on the firm order book; a 1,000 km/month single-core 3.3 kV plant is planned within 18 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance reiterated at INR4,300-4,500 crore; with INR1,722 crore in H1, this implies about INR2,580 crore in H2. Management expects about 60% of revenue in H2.
EBITDA margin expected to stay in 11-13% band until polymer plant is on stream; post polymer (by December 2027), management guided 14-16%.
Management expects order book to reach about INR2,500 crore of execution by March 2027 and expects 50% of next year's target in order book by end-Q3 and full next-year book by end-Q4.
EHV revenue targeted to reach double digit share of top line in Q3 and Q4 FY27.
Cash tax expected to start from Q1 2029 given carry-forward losses of INR1,432 crore at 31 March 2026.
Roadmap for 2028-2032 capacity (including plans for about five new MV lines a year from 2028) to be shared at end of Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: Polymer integrated complex: INR170 crore investment, total capacity 84,500 tons; Phase 1 (INR78 crore, 66,500 tons, captive) commissioning between June and December 2027. Phase 2 is an 18,000-ton peroxide XLPE line for 66-400 kV, commissioning early 2028. Project IRR stated at 30% post-tax; funding from INR78 crore QIP GCP account and INR100 crore internal accruals.
Sixth CCV line ordered with delivery within one year (buy-out from an international player's order); the standard lead time is about two years.
Copper cable capacity 1,500 tons/month live, being scaled to 2,500 tons/month.
LV cable project to be commissioned before April 2027; balancing equipment project INR75 crore; total additional capex about INR366 crore over six to seven projects.
Capacity utilisation approximately 45% of the level expected once the full balancing equipment is operational.
demand_pricing: Order inflow averages INR350-400 crore per month; Q3 and Q4 typically see higher inflow as government tenders are finalised.
Live enquiries of about INR32,000 crore for medium and extra high voltage cables expected to be finalised within 90 days, per management.
Adani Group entities are 43% of the order book; management stated Adani's share of top line is under 30% in Q2 and aims for a 20% cap over time, with orders at market price via reverse auction.

Pricing is price-variation linked with a 30-day lag to dispatch; management says a plus-minus of about 1% EBITDA impact arises from aluminium price swings. Contribution per tonne is stated to be protected.
Contribution margin as a percentage of revenue fell to 16.9% from 18.7% due to higher LME aluminium prices inflating the revenue base.
Data centre cable margin premium estimated at about 2% due to pre-qualification barriers. EHV vs MV margin differential estimated at 5-6%; EHV vs LV about 10%.
Export: UL approval applied for MV cables in the US; type-test samples sent for Europe; distributor in UAE and Middle East. Management expects a large export contribution in FY28.
HTLS market per management: about INR5,000 crore of tenders this year, with INR2,800-3,000 crore awarded; Diamond targets HTLS at no more than 5% of top line.

qa_highlights.question: How much FY28 revenue is backed by orders, and what is the order inflow momentum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the existing order book is valued at about INR4,300 crore at market prices and is targeted to yield about INR2,500 crore of revenue by March 2027; monthly inflow is INR350-400 crore with Q3 and Q4 seasonally stronger.

qa_highlights.question: Is data centre cable revenue sustainable, and what is the margin difference versus conventional cables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about INR750 crore from data centre customers in FY27 and cites 66 cities and more than 230 developers in scope. Margin premium is estimated at about 2% due to pre-qualification barriers.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q2 margin change is due to one-offs, and is the contract cost-plus?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts are price escalation based with a 30-day lag; falling metal prices lift percentage margin, and absolute contribution per unit is stable. No one-off costs were cited.

qa_highlights.question: What are the EBITDA margin expectations and capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 11-13% EBITDA margin until polymer is on stream, then 14-16% from next year; capacity utilisation is about 45% of the level expected after full balancing equipment is operational.

qa_highlights.question: What is the legacy receivable recovery status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legacy receivables are INR957 crore; it targets recovering INR300 crore within 24 months, of which INR116 crore is confirmed by customers so far.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax shield timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Carry-forward losses were INR1,432 crore at 31 March 2026; management expects cash tax to start in Q1 2029.

risks_watch: H2 revenue of about INR2,580 crore must be delivered to meet guidance; execution depends on Q3-Q4 order inflows and the seasonal tender cycle.
About 43% of the order book is Adani Group; concentration risk and the stated 20% cap timeline are not defined.
Metal price swings (aluminium, copper) affect percentage margins; a 30-day pass-through lag creates about 1% EBITDA variance per management.
Polymer Phase 1 commissioning in June-December 2027 and Phase 2 in early 2028 are key to the 14-16% margin target; delays would defer it.
Legacy receivables of INR957 crore with INR300 crore targeted for recovery over 24 months; only INR116 crore confirmed so far.
Management commentary on competition intensity, quality undercutting in the market, and the 2028-2032 capacity plan (to be detailed at Q4 FY27) remain open.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, data centre demand and polymer integration, with specific numeric targets. Less precise on FY28 capacity additions, the industry growth rate and the 2028-2032 roadmap, which were deferred to Q4.
key_quotes: Our revenue grew by 135%. Metal and price variation pass-through account for perhaps a third of that. The rest is real.
For us, quality is our brand, and that is why our employee and other expenses are 5.7% of revenue, and that is why our savings goes completely to the bottom line.
I can only tell you that the margin which we are having presently is the most reasonable margin which you should expect from us.
So EBITDA margins will always remain between 11% to 13%. Once our polymer gets on stream by December 2027, in the next year we will like to give you a band of 14% to 16%.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance of INR4,300-4,500 crore reiterated, implying ~INR2,580 crore in H2 (about 50% above H1's INR1,722 crore run-rate); backed by a INR3,735 crore firm order book (book-to-bill 1.29x), a 2,500 t/month data-centre copper line and ~INR750 crore expected data-centre revenue, though H2 step-up is large and only partly specified with capacity timing.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Margin guided at 11-13% until polymer is on stream, then 14-16% once polymer Phase 1 (INR78 crore, 66,500 t captive) commissions Jun-Dec 2027; Q2 EBITDA margin was 12.9% and management says margin rose ~240 bps, though part of that is falling metal prices lifting percentage margin.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Copper cable line already live at 1,500 t/month and being scaled to 2,500 t/month; LV cable project due before April 2027; polymer Phase 1 commissioning Jun-Dec 2027 and Phase 2 early 2028; capacity utilisation at about 45% of target once balancing equipment is operational.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 guidance of INR4,300-4,500 crore held, implying ~INR2,580 crore in H2 versus INR1,722 crore in H1 (about 50% step-up); firm order book INR3,735 crore (book-to-bill 1.29x) and ~INR750 crore data-centre revenue expected in FY27, though the H2 step-up is large.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only ~45% of target, but a 2028-2032 capacity roadmap (about five new MV lines a year from 2028) is to be shared at end Q4 FY27, and the solar cable plant (1,000 km/month) is planned within 18 months, with polymer Phase 2 (INR92 crore) also planned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 revenue guidance at INR4,300-4,500 crore rather than raising it, and H1 revenue is INR1,722 crore, so an upgrade would need H2 to clearly exceed the INR2,580 crore implied.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 must deliver about INR2,580 crore (50% above H1) and depends on Q3-Q4 order inflow (INR350-400 crore/month) and the seasonal tender cycle; polymer delays would defer the 14-16% margin target.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Sixth CCV line due within one year, solar 3.3 kV single-core cable plant planned within 18 months, and export products (UL approval applied for US MV cables; large export contribution expected in FY28).

rows.label: Order book converts to revenue by March 2027
rows.why: Management targets about INR2,500 crore of execution from the ~INR4,300 crore order book at market prices by March 2027, with H1 inflow of INR2,217 crore and monthly inflow of INR350-400 crore.

rows.label: EHV share to double digit in Q3/Q4 FY27
rows.why: Management targets EHV revenue at double-digit share of top line in Q3 and Q4 FY27, supported by INR974 crore AL59 800 kV HVDC order and ~INR32,000 crore of live MV/EHV enquiries expected to finalise within 90 days.

rows.label: Legacy receivable recovery
rows.why: Legacy receivables are INR957 crore with a target of INR300 crore recovered within 24 months, but only INR116 crore is customer-confirmed so far.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 guidance, data centre demand and the polymer-driven margin path, but cautious on FY28 capacity, the 2028-2032 roadmap and the Adani concentration (43% of order book); analysts pressed on margin sustainability and metal-price effects.
